summary.tldr: Raises the service rule for Governor General annuity and benefits to five consecutive years, with a medical exception.
what_it_does: Requires a Governor General to serve at least five consecutive years to qualify for a retiring annuity under the Governor General’s Act.
Deems a Governor General who cannot serve five years for medical reasons, in the opinion of the Governor in Council, to have met the five-year rule.
Bars money from the Consolidated Revenue Fund for administrative support or expense reimbursements for former Governor Generals who served less than five consecutive years.
Ends annuity payments under the old rules to former Governor Generals with less than five consecutive years of service when the bill comes into force, but keeps survivor payments going.
summary.background: The bill amends Part II of the Governor General’s Act, which deals with the retiring annuity and related benefits for a Governor General.
